speaker_role: unknown (Princeton Review presenter; test-prep company staff)
commercial_incentive: Princeton Review sells test prep and admissions services; the video promotes their channel and playlist.
key_insights: The main mistake is writing what you think admissions readers want instead of what you care about.
Ask yourself what makes you distinctly you, not what makes you interesting.
Small topics such as a reading nook or a favorite game work if you explain why they matter.
The reasons behind your choice reveal values, interests, and goals, which is what readers want to learn.
Show rather than tell, and reflect on challenges without sounding as though they define you.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Personal statement cap referenced as fewer than 650 words.
notable_or_distinctive: The reframing question 'what makes me me' versus 'what makes me interesting' is the one distinct idea.
reliability_notes: Short and general; the claim that this mistake keeps worthy candidates out is unsupported and the video is dated (6 years).
